display.purpose: The verdict word on the verdict field only; 50px below 760px.

display-figure.purpose: Days left on the verdict field; same voice at 48px for worklist counts and 28px in due lobes. Underlined when the deadline is soon.

body.purpose: Interface text and tables, tabular figures on.

label.purpose: Field labels and column heads, sentence case, normal tracking.

shadows.name: hairline-outline
shadows.purpose: Outline for cards, sheets, board, tab track, strip and resting filters; replaces borders.

shadows.name: highlight-hot
shadows.purpose: Ring in a highlight's own bright colour when its rule is hovered.

shadows.name: row-focus
shadows.purpose: Board row whose patient link has keyboard focus.

motion.name: overshoot
motion.purpose: 0.4s, small transforms only: button chip slide, press scale, filter chip crossing, area and chip lifts, disclosure chevron; and the coastline path morph.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: 0.4s for the verdict field recolour and the highlight sweep; 0.25s for the tab fill.

motion.name: hover-fade
motion.purpose: Colour, background, outline and opacity changes on hover.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Everything stops; highlights render in their final swept state; scroll-to-rule uses behavior auto.

breakpoints.name: stack
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: workspace and appeal grids become one column; gate unsticks.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: rail becomes an icon-only top bar, verdict field one column with 50px monuments, areas two per row, strip 2 by 2, board hides reason.

narrative.overview:
Every denial is an area on one map, and its verdict is the colour of the land. The system is a zoo-and-gardens guide map translated to dark: the map's cream water becomes a near-black ink-green ground, cream becomes the text, and the land keeps its flat, saturated colours. A biller reads the answer from the colour of a field before reading a word, then checks the evidence rule by rule against source documents set in the same single grotesk.

Colour is flat and unmodulated. There is no glow, grain or drop shadow; surfaces separate by tone and by 1px hairlines, and the big verdict field is divided from the dark ground by a drawn coastline rather than a border. Controls are capsules, and the primary capsule carries a round chip on its trailing edge. Small things that move take 0.4s and overshoot before they settle; colour changes ease out without overshoot.

Density is a working tool's density: a 232px rail, a rules column beside tabbed source sheets, and tables at 15px. The monumental type is reserved for two things only: the verdict word and the days-left figure.
keyCharacteristics: Five flat land colours, each bound to one verdict or status, on a near-black ink-green night ground.
Two tones per land: deep land with cream text at rest, bright land with ink text when selected or when the colour is the answer.
Colour always travels with its word (status capsules), never alone.
One grotesk (Hanken Grotesk, variable 100 to 900), tabular figures everywhere.
Coastlines and organic lobes divide; rectangles with borders do not.
Capsule controls with a round chip; 0.4s overshoot on small transforms only.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Each land colour means one verdict and its matching rule status; never use a land colour as decoration or as a generic accent.

rules.name: The Colour-Plus-Word Rule
rules.body: A status colour always appears with its word (Supports, Blocks, Missing docs, Not applicable, Appeal, Don't appeal yet, Ask the physician, Fix & resubmit, Not winnable, VOID). Colour alone never carries a status.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Land Rule
rules.body: Text on a bright land colour is ink; text on deep land or night is cream. Never put cream on bright land or ink on night.

rules.name: The Two Monuments Rule
rules.body: Only the verdict word and the days-left figure are set at display size; everything else stays at working size.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and headings are sentence case at normal tracking. The only all-caps word in the system is the VOID capsule.

rules.name: The Flat Land Rule
rules.body: Colour fills are flat: no gradients, glow, grain or drop shadow. Layered backgrounds exist only to drive the highlight sweep, and each layer is a single flat colour.

dos: Do bind every land colour to its verdict and status (land Appeal and Supports, coral Don't appeal yet and Blocks, sun Ask the physician and Missing docs, pond Fix & resubmit and verified quotes, lilac Not winnable).
Do pair every status colour with its word in a capsule.
Do keep findings on deep land with cream text and reserve the bright land with ink text for the selected rule and for fields where the colour is the answer.
Do divide the verdict field from the ground with a coastline, and divide strips and tables with 1px hairlines.
Do make controls capsules; give the primary a round chip on its trailing edge.
Do use the 0.4s overshoot (cubic-bezier(.34, 1.56, .64, 1)) only for small transforms and the coast morph, and ease-out (cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1)) for colour changes and the highlight sweep.
Do honour reduced motion: every animation and transition is switched off, the highlight lands in its final state, and scrolling to a rule jumps instead of smooth-scrolling.
Do lock export and mark VOID in coral whenever a quote does not match fetched text.
donts: Don't use gradients, glow, grain or drop shadows on fills.
Don't put cream text on bright land, or ink text on night.
Don't let colour carry a status without its word.
Don't add a second typeface; the hierarchy is weight and size within Hanken Grotesk.
Don't set anything but the verdict word and days figure at display size.
Don't use uppercase letter-spaced labels; VOID is the only all-caps word.
Don't overshoot colour, layout or large surfaces; overshoot is for chips, lifts, presses and the coast.
